summary: This House resolution expresses support for U.S. athletes competing in the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, commends Italy for hosting, and commits to security for the 2028 Los Angeles and 2034 Utah Games.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely ceremonial and expresses support for athletes without authorizing, appropriating, or directing any federal expenditures. Mentions of safety and security are aspirational and do not constitute spending policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No content addresses healthcare systems, coverage, or markets.
The resolution does not discuss firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration policy, visas, borders, or pathways.
The bill is silent on reproductive rights or abortion access.
While safety and security are mentioned, there is no engagement with military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces.
No environmental regulations, climate provisions, or energy policy appear in the text.
The resolution does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
The preamble notes that the Olympic movement has historically educated youth through athletics, but this is purely descriptive and does not alter federal education policy, funding, or structure.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
Safety and security language is general and does not touch sentencing, policing reforms, or criminal justice policy.
The bill contains no trade, tariff, or globalization measures.
No fiscal policy, deficit, or debt-reduction language is present.
The resolution does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The text thanks Italy for hosting but does not authorize, expand, or reduce foreign aid.
No election integrity, voting access, or electoral reform provisions exist.
The bill does not engage with technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No content addresses worker protections, union rights, or labor policy.
The resolution does not discuss religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
